overall:
The clumping agent's numbers are almost all right. Every static eigenvalue, threshold table (Gaussian and rational), unit conversion, Debt-3a recomputation and listed m=0 growth rate reproduces to printed precision. I used methods different from the agent's: brute-force 1D Nystrom against the Mehler closed form, a Cartesian secular equation from numerically diagonalized kernels, 3D tensor-grid power iteration, an l=0 Fourier-space operator (K = B^dag B), eigenvalues of the real linearized generator (van Kampen matrix) in each azimuthal sector, and first-order perturbation theory as an analytic anchor. The record numbers (37.7 um, 5.2 meV) match the source. The literature mostly checks out [S], with one wrong page range (Casti et al., Ann. N.Y. Acad. Sci. 867, 93-108, 1998) and two loose paraphrases.

The substantive error is in the dynamics. Growth was searched only in the gravity-coupled m=0 sector, and only off the imaginary axis. This missed purely growing gate-only m=+-1 modes: density-free, transverse-velocity-dipole, Weibel-like layering. These dominate past the parity-odd threshold, and the growth 'collapse' is a dip that recovers (1.2-1.5 per t_ff at G~/G = 1000-5000). C12's 'strong gating does not give fast growth' is therefore refuted, and C8, C11 and C20 need correction (MW fastest 0.88/t_ff at G~/G=280.7; cluster fastest modes differ, though phase mixing still wins there).

Evaluating the Kesden-Kamionkowski Sgr bound that the agent cited, at Sgr's relative speed, gives G~/G <~ 1-3 at v*=120 km/s (order of magnitude; the Sgr inputs are dagger memory). That is ten or more times below every velocity-selected threshold. So the long-range gated route is observationally excluded at the benchmark, not merely optional. For Paul's question this holds in every case: a perturbative velocity-dependent correction to gravity (G~ <= G) gives no velocity-selected instability (C9 confirmed), and the record's X cannot carry a long-range force (C16 confirmed). The obituary stands and is strengthened. All results here are [D] from executed scripts in a local homogeneous Jeans-swindle model, not [V]. No repository file was modified.
